transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... honestly, things have just been happening for months now, and I can't ignore it anymore. It's this pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around without me knowing, and the medical bills show up with all these errors. And then people just "forget" to call me back when I try to straighten it out. Everyone keeps telling me, "Oh, it's just administrative mistakes," or whatever, but... I know that's not true. I know they’re deliberately keeping information from me. They're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. It's just too consistent to be an accident.
Beyond the feeling that people are deliberately hiding information from you, have you been experiencing any unusual sensory perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others do not?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. It's just the paperwork, the appointments, the phone calls... the actual things happening right in front of me that I'm talking about. I'm not imagining things, I'm just looking at the facts.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or are you currently taking any medications?
No, I don't have any medical conditions. I'm... well, I'm not taking any medications either. My health is perfectly fine.
Do you feel that other people, perhaps outside of your sister's medical care, are also acting in ways that suggest they are trying to interfere with your life or sabotage you?

No, not at all. It's... it's really just the people involved in her care. I manage an office for a living, and everything at work is completely fine. My staff is great, my neighbors are normal. I don't think the whole world is out to get me or anything like that. 

It's very specifically the hospital administration, the billing department, the people handling her paperwork. That's where the interference is happening. Everything else in my life is perfectly normal, which is why this situation stands out so much.
Do you believe that the people at the hospital are working together in a coordinated, intentional group effort to target you specifically?

Yes, I do. I mean, for months now I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern with them. My sister’s appointments get moved without any notice, the bills show up wrong, and people constantly just... 'forget' to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me that it’s just normal administrative mistakes, but I know better. I know they’re keeping information from me on purpose and trying to push me out of the decisions regarding her care.
Have you ever tried to confront the hospital staff or administration directly with the evidence you have collected about these patterns?

I have, yes. I've brought it up during family meetings with the care team, and... well, those meetings have become pretty tense. They get very defensive when I point out the patterns. And honestly, it's starting to spill over a bit. At work, I've had a few uncomfortable conversations lately. I guess I've been pressing my staff harder about routine mistakes than I used to, just because I'm so on edge from dealing with the hospital. I'm still managing all my responsibilities at the office, but... I can tell it's starting to affect how people respond to me.

Do you feel that the hospital staff's actions are motivated by a specific, personal agenda they have against you, or is it more that you believe they are incompetent and trying to cover up their mistakes?

I don't think they're just incompetent. I mean, sure, everyone makes mistakes, but this... this is different. It feels very personal. They know exactly who I am and how involved I am in my sister's care. It's like they have a specific agenda to push me out, to keep me from asking questions or getting in their way. They aren't just covering up random errors; they are intentionally targeting me to make it impossible for me to manage her situation.

Are there any other situations in your life, besides the medical care for your sister, where you feel that specific individuals are intentionally acting to undermine your authority or prevent you from doing your job?

No, not really. It's just the hospital. Outside of dealing with my sister's appointments and trying to get straight answers from them, everything else is fine. I mean, I still keep my home in order, I pay my bills on time, and I do my job at the office. I know people might think I'm too focused on this whole hospital situation, but I'm not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. It's just this one specific issue where I know what they're doing.
Why do you think the hospital staff would want to go to such lengths to push you out of your sister's care?

I don't know the exact reason, honestly. I've thought about it a lot. Maybe it's because I'm the only one who actually reads the charts and asks the hard questions. I'm not just going to nod along when things don't add up. It could be that they're doing something... I don't know, maybe something unethical with her billing or her treatment plan, and they know I'm the one person who would catch it. Or maybe they just don't like being challenged by a family member who won't back down. All I know for sure is that they want me out of the picture, and they're working together to make it happen.
Do you feel that these individuals at the hospital have any special or unusual methods of communicating with each other, such as using secret codes, signals, or non-verbal cues that you have noticed?

No, I haven't noticed anything like secret codes or... signals. It's not like a spy movie. It's just normal conversations, but it's what they say and how they act when I'm around. They'll whisper to each other sometimes when they think I'm not looking, or they'll suddenly stop talking when I walk up to the nurse's station. But I don't think they're using, like, special hand signals or anything unusual like that. They're just regular people trying to keep me in the dark.
How long have you felt that the hospital staff has been working together in this coordinated way to push you out of your sister's care?

Well, it's been about 11 months now. That's when my sister's health suddenly got worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. Once I started doing that and really paying attention, that's when this whole thing with the staff began.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling unusually depressed, or having periods where you feel more energetic or irritable than is typical for you?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, I'm not depressed, and I don't have any strange bursts of energy or anything. I'm definitely stressed, and maybe a bit irritable sometimes, but... well, that's just because of everything going on with my sister and the staff. It's a very frustrating situation to deal with every day. But as far as my actual mood goes, no, it's just normal. I haven't noticed any real changes.
Have you attempted to report your concerns to any external authorities, such as a patient advocate, a hospital ombudsman, or a legal professional?

No, I haven't gone to anyone outside the hospital about it. I haven't called a lawyer or an ombudsman or anything like that. I guess I've just been so focused on managing my sister's day-to-day care and trying to handle the staff myself that I haven't taken that step.
